paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Hard times don't mean God has left the room. Paul tells the Thessalonians that all their persecution and affliction is "clear evidence of God's righteous judgment," and that they will be "counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are suffering" (2 Thessalonians 1:5). Your suffering for Jesus is not a sign you missed something. I think that's the kind of news a tired baker needs to hear.

Now hold on, because there's more. God sees what is done to His people, and Paul says it is "only right for God to repay with affliction those who afflict you, and to grant relief to you who are oppressed" (2 Thessalonians 1:6-7). The relief comes when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven, and on that day He comes "to be glorified in His saints and regarded with wonder by all who have believed" (2 Thessalonians 1:10). That's why my ovens stay ready. I don't know the day, and the Bible says only the Father does (Matthew 24:36), but I know Who is coming.

So how do you wait? Like the Thessalonians: faith growing, love increasing, and prayer going up the whole time. Paul prays that God will "count you worthy of His calling" and "powerfully fulfill your every good desire and work of faith" (2 Thessalonians 1:11). The Thessalonians don't hold on by their own muscle, friend. It all runs "according to the grace of our God and of the Lord Jesus Christ" (2 Thessalonians 1:12), and that grace holds you up when you can't hold yourself.
